headline: System One decision models show lower wrong-pick rates on a constructed legal-authority abstention test
summary: A University at Albany preprint compares four System One decision models with six generative language models on the CaseHOLD legal-reasoning benchmark. In a constructed abstention condition, the authors replace the correct holding with a similar real holding in 1,670 of 5,314 test items and add a “none” option. They report wrong-pick rates of 37.8–85.6% for generative models and 30.1–60.8% for decision models; the most cautious decision model also abstains on 26.2% of items where the correct holding remains. An agreement gate between a decision model and a generative model reportedly halves wrong citations on a held-out split. These are author-reported results from one English-language U.S. case-law task, not independent reproduction or evidence of legal reliability in practice.
